svg.title: The held GLM-5.3 flagship shipped its open weights after all — the gate turned out to be a license, not a hold, and the closed ceiling stayed frozen for a ninth straight brief
svg.desc: A two-lane diagram showing Z.ai's GLM-5.3 open-weights question resolving fully: both capability tiers are now open, but on divergent licenses. The top lane, shaded amber and marked "shipped, conditioned," is the GLM-5.3 flagship: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 60, a roughly 743-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts with about 39 billion active, tagged with vendor-claimed offensive-cyber capability. Its Hugging Face repository went from placeholder to a real downloadable checkpoint — an FP8 build near 756 gigabytes and a BF16 build near 1.5 terabytes — timestamped about 15:22 to 16:00 UTC on August 28, under a custom "glm-5.3" license rather than MIT, with a completed two-week safety review and a clause requiring any Model-as-a-Service operator above 10 billion dollars trailing-twelve-month revenue to pass a Z.ai security review before commercial use; running it needs an eight-GPU Hopper-or-newer node. A correction note states this supersedes the prior brief's "slip" call: the weights did land, essentially on the August 28 target, and the reporting has since caught up. The bottom lane, shaded teal and marked "shipped, MIT," is GLM-5.3-Flash, formerly the anonymous Ox Alpha endpoint: Index 57, a 320-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts with 18 billion active, natively multimodal, one-million-token context, shipped open under MIT on August 26. A center label states the danger gate did not block release — it shaped the license: the safe tier gets MIT, the frontier-adjacent cyber tier gets a bespoke, revenue-gated, safety-conditioned license. A footer notes the closed ceiling stayed frozen for a ninth straight brief — Claude Opus 5 at 63 remains number one and uncut at five and twenty-five dollars, no Index-64 model and no flagship price cut since July 24, now over five weeks — while Gemini 3.5 Pro stays absent on a third missed target and Meta's Watermelon holds an October date with a Hatch consumer-agent platform priced up to 199.99 dollars a month, still unreleased and unverified.
svg.text: The held flagship shipped — the gate was a license, not a hold
Aug-26 watch-item #1 resolves: both GLM-5.3 tiers are now open, but on divergent licenses — and Aug-29's "slip" call is superseded
↳ correction: this supersedes Aug-29's "slip" — the weights did land, ~on target; reporting has caught up
The danger gate didn't block release — it shaped the license: safe tier → MIT, cyber tier → bespoke, revenue-gated terms
Above the split, the closed ceiling still hasn't moved — 9th straight brief
❄️ Opus 5 = 63 (#1, uncut, $5/$25) · Fable 5 ~62 · GPT-5.6 Sol / Grok 4.6 ~61 · no Index-64 model · no flagship price cut since Jul 24 (>5 wks)
Gemini 3.5 Pro still absent (3rd missed target) · Meta "Watermelon" holds an October date + "Hatch" agent platform (up to $199.99/mo), still unreleased/unverified
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v4.1.1) · figures third-party unless tagged vendor-claimed · compiled Mon Aug 31 2026 (Los Angeles)
